body:
Can you explain what you're doing here?  

Is there an error with `no-func-assign`? Or are you saying there's an issue only when using your plugin?

Please provide as much detail as possible.

This is bug in `no-func-assign`. It's not related to my plugin (also happens when plugin not loaded). Eslint just crash with couple of projects that i tryed. If i disable `no-func-assign` in config, then everything works well.

First message contains exact description how to reproduce this bug.

Except this minor inconvenience, 0.8.0 release is very nice.
Can you narrow it down to a particular file in your project?

> First message contains exact description how to reproduce this bug.

No, it doesn't. It omits the content of the files eslint is being run on, which is exactly what we would need to reproduce this ourselves. If you run eslint on `/dev/null` with the same config, I'll bet you it doesn't crash.

This project contains only 5 js files, and all except index.js fail. Here are commands to run eslint on those files manually:

```
node node_modules/.bin/eslint --rulesdir lib ./lib/indent.js
node node_modules/.bin/eslint --rulesdir lib ./lib/no-async-aliases.js
node node_modules/.bin/eslint --rulesdir lib ./lib/no-lodash-aliases.js
node node_modules/.bin/eslint --rulesdir lib ./lib/no-wire-anonymous.js
```

Don't forget to edit `.eslintrc` prior to run eslint, because config disables `no-func-assign` to make thing work.

If you suspect, that problem is caused by my custom rule - disable `indent` in config and run without `--rulesdir`, it will fail too.

I can confirm this error.
When I lint the file foo.js with the following content eslint crashes:

``` js
// blank line here
var foo = module.exports = {};
```

If I remove the first blank line it works.

It seems the commit 9214c8c is the culprit (@btmills). If I revert this commit, everything works fine.

I debugged this a bit, in `getScope`  I have noticed a strange `scopeMap`:

```
scopeMap [ , 0 ]
```

As the first item in `scopeMap` is undefined, I’ll get `undefined` as scope returned.

It looks like `max-len` and `no-func-assign` are incompatible for some reason. Try running `eslint test.js --reset --rule 'max-len: [2, 80, 4]' --rule 'no-func-assign: 2'` where `test.js` has a comment or blank line before the first source line. _Edit: Removing the `max-len` flag will cause everything to work fine._

rename.from: no-func-assign rule crash eslint if not disabled

issue.body: In #1224 we discovered a bug where a rule modified an AST node which is passed to that rule. To prevent such bugs we could freeze the AST nodes or passing just a copy to the rules.
